entries.definition: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty where *older* is merely comparative, presenting advanced years as a settled condition rather than a point on a scale.

entries.definition: growing old
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling of the same word, carrying the identical sense of decline already under way.

entries.definition: growing old
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts age in motion rather than in place - the process, not the state - and that forward motion carries its faint edge of decline.

entries.definition: very old
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pure intensification — *old* taken to its limit, and the size of the exaggeration is what gives it its edge.

entries.definition: of or like a feeble old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal in shape but withering in effect, covering both actually being a feeble old woman and merely resembling one, with the contempt built into the word rather than the sentence.

entries.definition: being at least 100 years old
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely quantitative — it fixes a number where *ancient* only gestures at extremity, and passes no verdict with it.

entries.definition: (of fabrics and paper) grown dark in color over time
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The one member describing what time does to the colour of a material rather than to a life, and it carries no judgement at all.
examples: the darkened margins of the paper

entries.definition: mentally or physically infirm with age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous where *aged* is not, making the infirmity — of mind or of body — the whole of what it says about the person.
examples: his mother was doddering and frail

entries.definition: mentally or physically infirm with age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same verdict of age-borne infirmity as *doddering*, its shorter form making the mockery sound offhand rather than deliberate.
examples: his mother was doddering and frail

entries.definition: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The courteous way to say advanced in years, gentler in force than *aged* and careful to claim nothing further about the person.
examples: elderly residents could remember the construction of the first skyscraper

entries.definition: mentally or physically infirm with age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and blunt — the same infirmity as *doddering*, named in a word too flippant to leave the person any dignity.

entries.definition: having attained a specific age; (‘aged’ is pronounced as one syllable)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a threshold reached, with none of the weight of accumulated years that *aged* brings with it.

entries.definition: (used especially of persons) having lived for a relatively long time or attained a specific age
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unloaded, and it holds both readings at once — a long life lived or simply a stated age attained — where *of age* carries only the second.

entries.definition: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A comparative doing the work of a plain description, which is what makes it the softest term here — it implies a scale instead of naming a state.

entries.definition: growing old
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical and detached: it states the same growing old as *aging* in a register that declines to feel anything about it.

entries.definition: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Carries a note of standing rather than decline, making it the one flattering way in this set to say advanced in years.

entries.definition: expecting a rise in prices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional rather than evaluative: it names an expectation that prices will rise, taking no view of the person holding it the way *optimistic* does.

entries.definition: pleasantly (even unrealistically) optimistic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Leads with the pleasantness and leaves the unrealism in the background, where *pollyannaish* brings it to the front.

entries.definition: expecting the best in this best of all possible worlds
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unmarked term for expecting the best, and the only one here that neither congratulates the expectation nor doubts it.

entries.definition: pleasantly (even unrealistically) optimistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hangs its whole weight on the unrealistic half of the same pleasant optimism, so the good cheer itself becomes the failing.

entries.definition: reflecting optimism
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the optimism into what is being shown rather than into the one holding it, so it colours a view instead of judging a temperament.
examples: looked at the world through rose-colored glasses

entries.definition: reflecting optimism
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The shorter, warmer form beside *rose-colored*, and the readier of the two to stand as simple praise for how a prospect looks.
examples: looked at the world through rose-colored glasses

entries.definition: confidently optimistic and cheerful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds steadiness to the cheer: confidence held, not merely expectation entertained, which is what lifts it past *optimistic*.

entries.definition: confidently optimistic and cheerful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The heavier, more formal twin of *sanguine* for the same confident cheer, the weight falling on the word rather than the mood.

entries.definition: unrealistically or naively optimistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Marks the optimism as a fault either way — whether it has outrun the facts or never met them — and the dreaminess is the point.

entries.definition: pleasantly (even unrealistically) optimistic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Buoyant and forward-leaning where *cheerful* is merely pleasant, and it carries the least doubt of the three.

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disarray or confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of a thing thrown into disarray rather than snapped in two - the confusion reads as damage done to it, not merely order gone missing.

entries.definition: lacking a visible order or organization
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sharpens the charge into a spectacle - not a trace of order or organization to be seen, where *disorganized* merely notes the lack.

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disarray or confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the muddle in the thing itself rather than in anyone's head - it is the arrangement that is tangled, not a mind.
examples: a confused mass of papers on the desk

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disarray or confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of these - it records that order has given way to disarray and stops there, where *broken* wants you to feel the blow.

entries.definition: lacking order or methodical arrangement or function
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries exactly the force of *disorganized*; the spelling is the whole of the difference.

entries.definition: lacking order or methodical arrangement or function
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's plain statement of the fault - order, methodical arrangement and working function all simply absent, with none of the wreckage *chaotic* pictures.
examples: a thousand pages of muddy and disorganized prose
she was too disorganized to be an agreeable roommate

entries.definition: snarled or stalled in complete confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Coarse and total - a snarl or dead stop treated as a botch someone is answerable for, the harshest word in the family.

entries.definition: lacking a visible order or organization
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Its jingling shape makes the same invisible order sound hectic and headlong, far lighter in judgement than *chaotic*.

entries.definition: thrown together in a disorderly fashion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the making rather than the thing: pieces flung together in haste, so the disorder sits in how it was put together.

entries.definition: snarled or stalled in complete confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the same total snarl-up or standstill with a clipped, almost breezy label - rueful where *fucked-up* is furious.

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disorganization or incoherence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sounds the same collapse as an unmaking, graver and more final than *unstuck* - the thing not merely loosened but ruined.

entries.definition: not efficient or methodical
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coolest reproach here - it faults the missing method and the inefficiency that comes with it, and pictures no wreckage at all.
examples: the project failed through unmethodical planning

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disorganization or incoherence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pictures the collapse as a coming-apart - what was holding gives way, and the disorganization or incoherence follows from that.
examples: price programs became unstuck because little grain was available

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disarray or confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pictures the disarray as a tipping-over: the arrangement knocked out of place rather than destroyed, and the upheaval still fresh.

entries.definition: radically new or original
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval for newness pushed to its edge, where the break with what came before is the whole of the claim - a bigger assertion than *fresh* makes.

entries.definition: radically new or original
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises the same radical newness as *avant-garde* but hears nerve in it, as though the thing is new because someone risked making it so.

entries.definition: done by hand without mechanical aids or devices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a statement of method - the hand working without mechanical aid or device - and it carries none of the approval the words beside it do.

entries.definition: done by hand without mechanical aids or devices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Says exactly what *freehand* says and no more, still describing how a thing was done rather than passing any judgement on it.

entries.definition: original and of a kind not seen before
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of the three that share this sense: not merely without precedent but welcome for it, where *new* only records the absence.

entries.definition: containing seeds of later development
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise pointed forward - the thing is valued for the later development it holds in seed, not for what it already amounts to.

entries.definition: being or producing something like nothing done or experienced or created before
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most emphatic way to say it - first through unbroken ground - where *innovative* states the same feat without the flourish.

entries.definition: being or producing something like nothing done or experienced or created before
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The dry variant of *innovative*, sounding more like a classification of the thing than any compliment paid to it.
examples: a mind so innovational, so original
